maths_errors.text: Cone and pyramid volumes are one-third of the corresponding prism or cylinder with the same base.
maths_errors.correction: Incomplete condition. A cone or pyramid has one-third of the volume of the prism or cylinder with the same base AND the same perpendicular height. Without equal heights the statement is false. slides[3].mistakes[2].correction states the condition correctly ('same base and height'), so the two places disagree.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Additional foundation: surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids
missing_spec_content.why: Surface area is not taught for any solid. The lesson only says 'Surface area is a different calculation (sum of all face areas)'. The curved surface area of a cone (πrl, with slant height l) and the surface area of a sphere (4πr²) are absent.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Additional foundation: surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids
missing_spec_content.why: Composite solids are not mentioned at all. An example would be a cylinder topped with a hemisphere, where the volume is found by adding or subtracting parts.
Frustums (a large cone minus a small cone) are not taught.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Basic foundation: know and apply formulae to calculate: area of triangles, parallelograms, trapezia
missing_spec_content.why: The triangle area appears only in passing in keyFacts[1].examTip. Areas of parallelograms and trapezia, which are needed for prism cross-sections, are not taught.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Basic foundation: know the formulae: circumference of a circle = 2πr = πd ... calculate perimeters of 2D shapes, including circles areas of circles and composite shapes
missing_spec_content.why: Circumference, perimeter and areas of composite 2D shapes are not taught. πr² appears only as a step inside the cylinder formula.

density.text: Cuboid: V = l × w × h  |  Any prism: V = area of cross-section × length  |  Cylinder: V = πr²h  |  Cone: V = ⅓πr²h  |  Sphere: V = (4/3)πr³  |  Pyramid: V = ⅓ × base area × height
density.why: Six formulae are packed into one line separated by bars. A first-time learner cannot take them all in at one read.

density.text: Cone and pyramid volumes are one-third of the corresponding prism or cylinder with the same base.
density.why: The fact is stated with no reason or illustration. The new idea of comparing with a 'corresponding' shape is left unexplained.

density.text: A cylinder is a circular prism, so its volume follows exactly the same logic — you just need the area of the circular face first.
density.why: One sentence carries three ideas: a cylinder is a prism, the prism rule applies, and you must find the circle area first.

density.text: The volume of the cylinder is 176π cm³ (≈ 552.9 cm³).
density.why: The decimal value appears without its step (176 × π = 552.92…, rounded to 1 d.p.).
